subject: Token-drip elongation: customer advisory and immediate mitigations
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena@bigtide.io>, BigTide Ops <support@bigtide.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Token-drip elongation: customer advisory and immediate mitigations

Hi Elena / BigTide team,

Quick heads-up from Redwood Ops: between 09:40–10:05 PDT this morning we observed elevated per-token emission latency for streaming chat endpoints used by BigTide (your traffic routed to us in us-west-2). Symptoms looked like a "drip" pattern where tokens arrive in smaller, irregular batches and overall response completion time stretched by 40–250% at the p95/p99.

What we're doing now:
- Mitigating: we pushed a temporary routing tweak to route affected sessions to a stable kernel profile (completed at 09:58).
- Short-term guidance for your app (immediately helpful):
  • If you rely on streaming progress bars, fallback to non-streamed calls for long replies.
  • Increase client-side stream buffer timeout to 6s (was 2–3s) to avoid premature retry storms.
  • For websocket clients: enable small exponential backoff on reconnects (100ms -> 200ms -> 400ms).

Initial impact estimate: roughly 2.3% of BigTide’s interactive requests hit the degraded path during the window; users with long-turn prompts saw the bulk of the effect.

Root-cause hypothesis (work in progress): a mismatch in kernel selection for a small subset of our older GPU hosts combined with a KV cache eviction pattern under a short-lived traffic spike. That caused the runtime to fall back to a slower emission path for affected streams. We have an active engineering runbook and are executing a targeted fix (details below).

Immediate next actions (we own these):
- Full rollout of a kernel selection rollback to the last-known-good profile (ETA 2 hours).
- Telemetry deep-dive and attachment of incident timeline; we will share a consolidated timeline and remediation notes within 24h.
- Offer to apply a transient credit for observable user-impact; will propose amount once we finish scope analysis.

Would you prefer we schedule a quick call now (15–20m) to walk through mitigations, or should we proceed with the plan and send a written post-incident summary?

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (partial), mitigation_patch_v1.diff (test-only patch)

Apologies for the disruption — we recognize this is impacting user experience and we are treating it as high priority.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0173

From: Elena Martin <elena@bigtide.io>

1) Any idea on how long until the rollback is finished? We have customers on demos right now and the elongated replies are causing user confusion.
2) Weʼll need an initial estimate of impacted requests (rough number) and an early take on a credit/compensation rhythm so I can prep Finance.

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Token-drip elongation: customer advisory and immediate mitigations

Folks — copying internal ops plan. Elena asked for timeline and credit estimate. Proposed immediate plan below (we should align before I reply):

Plan (0–3h):
- Push kernel-selection rollback to all affected edge pools (Markus). Validate token pacing on canary (10 min) then global (staged over 45m).
- Temporarily pin BigTide to stable model variant on us-west-2 (Laura).
- Increase kv_cache retention window by 30s to reduce eviction churn (Mina).
- Prepare credit estimate: use traffic slice from 09:40–10:05 and p95 slowdown multiplier; propose credit draft.

Longer term (post-mortem):
- Add guardrail to prevent kernel fallback in latency-sensitive stream paths.
- Expand telemetry to expose token emission histograms by routing key.

Markus — can you confirm the rollback command and if there are any risk flags? Mina — prepare the timeline CSV and quick diff for the kv_cache tweak; Iʼll assemble the credit draft.

— Laura

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena@bigtide.io>
Cc: BigTide Ops <support@bigtide.io>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token-drip elongation: customer advisory and immediate mitigations

Hi Elena — quick status and summary now that the remediation is in: 

What we changed (completed):
- 09:58 PDT: Canary rollback of kernel-selection to last-known-good profile for the streaming runtime. Canary validated token emission profiles (p50/p95) within expected baselines.
- 10:45 PDT: Global rollout completed.
- 10:47 PDT: KV cache retention window increased by 30s for us-west-2.

Impact & scope:
- Observed window: 09:40–10:05 PDT.
- Affected BigTide sessions: ~2.3% of interactive streaming requests (our traffic slice). Of those, 0.4% had end-user visible timeouts triggered by client retry logic.

Customer-facing mitigations we recommend (finalized):
- For websocket clients: adopt 200–500ms initial backoff on stream reconnects and cap retries to 3 in 60s.
- For all clients: implement a short client-side debounce to coalesce micro-chunks into a single UI update (reduces perceived jitter).
- Where reproducibility is a concern: temporarily route heavy long-turn users to non-streaming completions (more predictable until we ship the long-term fix).

Post-incident deliverables we will provide by Tue EOD (13 Apr):
- Consolidated incident timeline (CSV attached).
- Root cause analysis draft and engineering remediation plan.
- Proposed customer credit: draft attached (credit_offer_draft.pdf).

Apology and next steps: we appreciate your patience. We're prioritizing this fix in our serving runtime roadmap so it doesn't recur; long-term items include better kernel-compatibility checks and token-emission SLO alarms. Would you like an hour-long review with our infra and product engineering teams this week to walk the RCA and longer-term mitigations?

— Dylan

From: Elena Martin <elena@bigtide.io>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, BigTide Ops <support@bigtide.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token-drip elongation: customer advisory and immediate mitigations

Thanks — thatʼs helpful and appreciated. The logs line up with your window. Weʼd like to take the credit draft to Finance; can you confirm the calculation method briefly in the RCA (we prefer the traffic-slice p95 delta approach you referenced).

Please schedule the 1h review for Thursday morning PST; invite product + infra. Weʼll also send a short list of example sessions where the behavior was most visible so you can cross-check with traces.

Appreciate the rapid response and the pragmatic mitigations — looking forward to the RCA.

— Elena
